tells: The piece uses captured photogrammetry or point-cloud data of real streets, deliberately corrupted, and the corruption has a theme: simulation, memory and code.

defects: Dot-matrix letterforms are rough: counters and diagonals in R, M, N, S, G and the '$' that should be an S break up, so words like HARBOUR and GONE read as noisy rather than as designed glyphs
In the 1/6 s pairs, words appear by cutting on in place (TIDE pops in whole next to LOW) with no build, no light-up order and no settle
The water plate is a stretched, smeared horizontal blur that reads as a low-res texture moving linearly, not as water with highlights or depth
The frame is underexposed overall: sky and water collapse into near-black blue mush, and the horizon and pier silhouettes are barely there
Stray single dots and small clusters (lower right in frame 1, left edge in frame 3) look like leftover particles rather than deliberate accents
The scattered-lights frame at ~40% is mostly empty dark sky: dead air in the composition
The reflection of ON is a straight mirrored copy with no ripple distortion and is cropped by the frame edge
There are only 2 shots across 20 s, and most text sits on a slow drift with little camera language
gaps: Choreography: the lights should behave like lights, turning on in a sequence along the stroke, flickering on with overshoot and decaying glow, swarming in from the harbour and settling. Right now words pop or fade in place with linear drift and no weight or follow-through

Pacing and arc: two long shots carry about 17 s at a flat level of energy. The real lift (the warm colour shift and the ON hit at about 17.3 s) comes at about 87%, too late and too brief to work as a peak and release. There are no cuts or camera moves to match the music's sections at about 3 s, 7 s and 12 s

Finish and world: the custom dot type needs proper grid-fitted glyphs, plus bloom with real falloff and slightly uneven bulbs. The harbour needs readable values: moonlit water with specular highlights, depth haze, and reflections that ripple. As it stands the night scene is a dark smear with no light design
